elements.element: The cap amount is determined using a greater-of formulation between two alternative limbs.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 limits liability to “the greater of (a) ... and (b) USD 1,000,000.”

elements.element: The first cap limb equals fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim.
elements.evidence: The clause uses “all amounts paid or payable ... under this Agreement and all Order Forms,” which is broader than fees, and measures the period before the event giving rise to the claim rather than before the claim.

elements.element: The second cap limb is USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 expressly provides a USD 1,000,000 second limb.

result.reason: The redline creates a mutual greater-of cap with a USD 1,000,000 floor, but its first limb is not strictly limited to fees and uses a different timing trigger. More importantly, the operative text supplied does not define “Excluded Claims,” so none of the required carve-outs is demonstrably present. It also omits the mutual indirect/consequential-damages exclusion and the payment-obligations clarification. The fallback is not met because the cap is not equal to 12 months' fees and its required carve-outs are likewise unsubstantiated. The amendment does not appear to disturb unrelated commercial terms, but it is not minimal toward any complete playbook level because substantial required language remains omitted.
